title: MV/MZ Visual Event Editor - a node-based eventing tool

posts.author: Drag
posts.body:
VISUAL EVENT EDITOR
v0.1.135 BETA
by Drag & Plugin
A node-based eventing tool for RPG Maker MV & MZ.
​
Overview
Visual Event Editor
is a node-based eventing tool for
RPG Maker MV and MZ
. It transforms the native list of event commands into an intuitive graph interface, making event creation faster, clearer, and easier to maintain.
Designed for both beginners and advanced users, it brings modern visual scripting concepts to the RPG Maker ecosystem, while maintaining compatibility with the native editor and plugins.
Features
Node-Based Event Creation
Compatible with RPG Maker MV, MZ and plugins
In-Graph Search
(
Ctrl + F
) and
Advanced Search
(find references across all events and maps)
Reroute Nodes
for cleaner curves layout
Comment & Group Boxes
with customizable color, text and size
Automatic Node Layout
for a clean graph organization with the press of a button
Live Playtesting
of events or specific commands selections
Execution Highlighting
for easier debug.
Automatic Node Conversion of MZ Plugins Commands
Custom Node Framework
(WIP)
Notetag Manager
for clear and easy notes and notetags manipulation
Move Route Preview for MV
(+ fixes and improvements for MZ)
Automatic Backups
on save (optional)
Automatic Save
with customizable interval (optional)
Various QOL
over the native editor, e.g. resizable windows/inputs and command search
Extended Self-Switches
from A-D to A-Z
Event page naming
Unlimited common, map and troop events
Unlimited switches and variables
Screenshots
Custom nodes
The editor supports extensibility through custom nodes.
You can create and distribute your own custom nodes without modifying the core editor. Custom nodes are automatically detected and integrated into the editor.
More documentation will be provided in future updates as the framework is completed. This is still a work in progress.
How to Use
Installation :
Download the latest version from this page.
Extract the archive.
Copy the folders into your RPG Maker project root (where
Game.rmmzproject
or
Game.rmmvproject
is located).
Open RPG Maker MV or MZ.
Add & enable
Drag_VisualEvent.js
in the Plugin Manager.
Start a playtest to launch the Visual Event Editor.
List of controls & shortcuts are available on the itch.io/github page.
Plugin Commands / Script Calls / Plugin Parameters
None. Parameters/settings can be customized directly within the editor window.
Download
https://github.com/DragAndPlugin/Visual-Event-Editor
https://drag-and-plug-in.itch.io/visual-event-editor

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Absolute madlad.
I'd love to see how this improves over the regular event editor. There is certainly a lot of be desired about the basic event editor, but it is "visual" more than programming in, for example, Unity.
Would be great if there was a tutorial video not necessarily about how to use the plugin (though that's a bonus too) but to show how it can improve workflow in RM.
I'd be curious to know how well it can create some sort of mechanic by simplifying the usage of plugin commands, scripts, and of course event commands.
And how that might be integrated (and later modified) within the RM editor itself.

Click to expand...
Indeed, the native editor also use "visual eventing". Its list of event commands is however, for me, very difficult to read when there is dozens of entries and/or (nested) conditional branches.
A couple years ago, I started learning Unreal and discovered their Blueprints (which were my first visual scripting tool). I found it so intuitive and easy to read that it inspired me to develop this plugin.

I will probably do a showcase video at some point, but I'm absolutely terrible at recording and I have absolutely no skill in video editing. So that will have to wait a bit !
In the meantime, I can tell you that I've tried to design it to be as intuitive as possible and to integrate as much QOL as possible, from a simple search command to the automatic generation of label/jump label in non-linear execution flow. And there is more to come in the future !
